name: Mass Layoff / Reduction in Force (RIF)
description: Workforce reduction response structure. Activates when a mass layoff, reduction in force, or large-scale restructuring is approved by board/CEO. Emphasizes legal compliance (WARN Act), human dignity, notification sequencing, and organizational continuity.
trigger_conditions: Board approves reduction in force affecting 10%+ or 50+ employees
Funding round fails and cash runway requires immediate headcount reduction
Merger or acquisition requires duplicate role elimination (above WARN thresholds)
Pandemic / market crash requires emergency downsizing
Pivot or shutdown of major product line or business unit
Site or facility closure requiring mass employee notification
Offshoring or outsourcing decision affecting large team

responsibilities: Overall decision authority on RIF scope, timing, and messaging
Final approval on severance package design
Deliver all-hands message and represent organizational direction
Approve impacted employee list after legal and HR review
Accept accountability for the decision — own the narrative
Set tone for remaining team — retention and motivation
Design notification sequencing — managers → impacted → retained → public
Coordinate logistics for notification day (rooms, IT access, security)
Manage facility operations — entry/exit, badge collection, equipment return
Business continuity planning — which roles are critical post-RIF
Workload redistribution among retained employees
Ensure payroll, benefits, and IT access transition timelines are executed

comms_lead.role: CMO (internal communications) + Head of HR (individual notifications)
responsibilities: [CMO] Draft all-hands email, FAQ, and public statement (if applicable)
[CMO] Manage timing of communications — no leaks before manager notifications
[CMO] Coordinate with PR if layoff is newsworthy (public company, large numbers)
[HR] Lead one-on-one notification meetings with impacted employees
[HR] Prepare separation packets (severance agreement, benefits info, COBRA)
[HR] Manage benefits transitions — health insurance, stock vesting, 401(k)
[HR] Coordinate EAP (Employee Assistance Program) access for impacted employees
WARN Act compliance — 60-day advance notice (US), state-level WARN laws (CA, NY, etc.)
Review impacted employee list for disparate impact discrimination risk
Prepare separation agreements and release of claims
Advise on COBRA, continuation coverage, and benefits compliance
Ensure compliance with international employment laws for global workforce
Advise on public disclosure obligations (SEC for public companies)
Review retention agreements for key employees being retained

key_actions: 1. Legal review of WARN Act compliance — 60-day notice required (US). Check state-level WARN (CA: 60-day, NY: 90-day for certain cases)
2. Design notification sequence: Managers notified first (morning) → Impacted employees (mid-day, same day) → Retained (late day) → Public (after close)
3. NEVER notify on a Friday — best days are Tuesday through Thursday. Avoid Monday (start-of-week panic) and Friday (no support access over weekend)
4. Severance package design — minimum statutory, target competitive: 4-12 weeks salary + 1 week per year of service, COBRA coverage period, outplacement services
5. Notification logistics — private rooms, HR + manager paired for each impacted employee, 15-minute meetings, security escort if needed for access revocation
6. IT access revocation plan — revoke at time of notification, not before. Capture all company data. Coordinate with IT to avoid accidental lockout of retained employees
7. Retained employee communication — why them, new roles, workload plan, morale support. They will be scared and need reassurance immediately
8. EAP (Employee Assistance Program) activation — available for both impacted and retained employees. Grief, stress, and career transition counseling
9. Benefits transition — COBRA paperwork, 401(k) rollover information, unvested equity treatment (acceleration policy), final paycheck timing by state law
10. Outplacement services — engage firm (Lee Hecht Harrison, RiseSmart, etc.), resume support, career coaching, networking access
11. Public statement preparation — if required (public company with securities filing, or large enough to attract press). Do not use euphemisms ('streamlining,' 'synergies'). Own the decision
12. Manager training in advance — how to deliver the message, what to say/not say, how to handle emotional responses, what to do if employee becomes distressed

communication_protocol.internal: Strict sequencing: Managers (before impacted) → Impacted employees (individual notification meetings, same day) → Retained employees (all-hands same day). CEO owns all-hands message. No advanced notice to anyone outside need-to-know (legal, HR, ops). Leak prevention is critical — accidental advance notice can trigger panic and legal exposure.
communication_protocol.external: Public statement only if legally required (SEC filing, WARN notice) or inevitable (press will find out). Factual, dignified, no euphemisms. No interviews with departing employees. No discussion of specific severance terms publicly.
communication_protocol.cadence: Notification day: Hourly standup with ops, IT, HR, legal. Following week: Daily HR standup for transition status. Weekly retained employee pulse check for 90 days.

escalation_timeline.t_minus_60d: WARN Act notice filed (US) — start 60-day clock
escalation_timeline.t_minus_4wk: Impacted employee list finalized → Legal/HR review for disparate impact → IT access plan designed
escalation_timeline.t_minus_2wk: Severance packages finalized → Manager briefing materials prepared → Notification logistics confirmed
escalation_timeline.t_minus_1wk: Managers trained → IT access revocation scripts tested → Separation packets printed
escalation_timeline.t0_notification_day: AM: Managers notified → Mid-day: Impacted employees notified individually → PM: Retained all-hands → After close: Public statement (if needed)
escalation_timeline.t1_4wk: Transition period — knowledge transfer, final pay, benefits transition, outplacement begins
escalation_timeline.t30_90d: Retained employee pulse check → Org design stabilization → Backfill decisions for critical gaps → Post-RIF culture assessment
